steps: The potential at the surface of the sphere is V(R) = kQ/R = 16 V.
For a solid sphere, the potential at an internal point (r ≤ R) is V(r) = (kQ / 2R) * (3 - r^2/R^2).
At point P (r = R/2), the potential is V(P) = (kQ / 2R) * (3 - 1/4) = (11/8) * (kQ/R).
Substituting kQ/R = 16 V, we get V(P) = (11/8) * 16 = 22 V.
At point S (r = 2R), the potential is V(S) = kQ / (2R) = (1/2) * (kQ/R) = 8 V.
The potential difference between P and S is V(P) - V(S) = 22 - 8 = 14 V.
